about.title: Paradise Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Paradise sits on a ridge with a mix of small businesses, rebuilt storefronts, and rural properties along corridors like Clark Road and Pentz Road, and uneven surfaces, wet floors, and poorly lit walkways can cause serious falls in any of these settings. If you were hurt on someone else's property here in Butte County, California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard that caused your fall and failed to fix it or warn you. That's why documentation matters so much: photos of the spot, the condition of the flooring or steps, and any surveillance footage from the property can make the difference in a claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney in our network who can look at what happened, explain your options, and take on your case if it makes sense for you.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Paradise Premises Liability Claim

items.title: Proving the Owner Had Notice
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather evidence, like maintenance logs or prior complaints, to establish that notice.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Footage Early
items.desc: Many Paradise businesses record over surveillance video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request and preserve that footage can be critical to showing what actually happened.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your percentage of fault but isn't automatically barred. An attorney can help present your side clearly so fault is assessed fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Paradise?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government entity, like the Town of Paradise, owns or maintains the property, the deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim filing requirement. Because of this, it's best to have your situation reviewed as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the store or business says I was partly at fault?
items.answer: That doesn't automatically end your claim. California's comparative fault rule allows you to still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility, though the amount may be adjusted accordingly. An attorney can help gather evidence to show the property owner's role in the hazard.

items.question: Are falls in Paradise usually connected to specific properties or areas?
items.answer: Falls can happen anywhere property isn't properly maintained, from parking lots along Skyway to walkways near Clark Road businesses. There's no single pattern; each case comes down to the specific conditions and whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. That's why documenting the scene right after a fall is so important.
